title: Sweden 1740-1777: the price of the riksdaler specie in marks kopparmynt, and the Riksbank's notes and metal reserves (annual)
source: Sveriges riksbank, Historical Monetary and Financial Statistics for Sweden: Volume I, ch. 4 (R. Edvinsson, 'The multiple currencies of Sweden-Finland 1534-1803', 2010), Table I.A4.7 'Riksdaler in mark 1534-1776'; Volume II, ch. 8 (K. Fregert, 'The Riksbank balance sheet, 1668-2011', 2014), Table II.A8.1 'Riksbank assets 1668- in SEK' (column 'Reserves: metal') and Table II.A8.2 'Riksbank liabilities and equity 1668- in SEK.' (column 'Notes')
series: riksdaler_marks: the annual average price of the riksdaler (specie) in marks kopparmynt, with the lowest (riksdaler_low) and highest (riksdaler_high) quotation of the year (Table I.A4.7; the row for 1777 has the average only). notes_sek and metal_reserves_sek: the Riksbank's notes outstanding and its metal reserves at the end of the year, in SEK at the book's conversion (Fregert 2014, Table 8.1: 1 daler silvermynt = 1/6 SEK to 1777; 1 riksdaler specie = 1 SEK in 1777-1788)
license: Sveriges riksbank's terms for its open data: 'The Riksbank's open data is freely available and may be further used without any special consent or agreement being required. Enter source, Sveriges riksbank and date. If you have processed statistics taken from the Riksbank's website, you may not state Sveriges Riksbank as the source.' The snapshot stores the values as published (source: Sveriges riksbank, 2026-10-15). The ratios the chapter computes from them (the riksdaler against its par of 36 marks; metal reserves against notes) are the book's own calculations and are attributed to the book and to Edvinsson (2010) and Fregert (2014), not to the Riksbank.
notes: Par: 36 marks kopparmynt = 3 daler silvermynt to the riksdaler, the parity the Caps tried to restore in 1766; the reform of 1776 fixed 1 riksdaler = 6 daler silvermynt = 72 marks kopparmynt (Edvinsson 2010, pp. 180-183, bullion_facts rows ed_caps and ed_1776), which is the value of 1777 in Table I.A4.7. The units of the balance sheet differ from Edvinsson's text: the notes of 1743 in Table II.A8.2 (2,380,216 SEK, or about 14.3 million daler silvermynt at 1 daler silvermynt = 1/6 SEK) are not Edvinsson's '9.5 million daler silvermynt' for 1743 (row ed_1743), which rests on another source (Sjostrand 1909); the chapter does not compare the two levels and uses the balance sheet only for changes and for the ratio of metal reserves to notes, which do not depend on the unit.
